doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Space in music and Miles Davis
summary: Noto and Menza on the importance of space, with Miles as the example.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I think the space in music is just as important as the notes. You know you get a person like, an individualist and an innovator like Miles Davis, I mean he played one note and the beat’s going on, and he waited, and made you hear a bunch of other notes.
You would lean forward waiting for the next — trying to guess where he was going to put it.
Space is important then, you know?
